facts_sources.title: Rock dove - Wikipedia
facts_sources.used_for: overview, plumage, size, native and introduced range, habitat, behaviour, voice (coo, alarm, nest call, juveniles, display with inflated throat and bowing), crop milk

facts_sources.title: IOC World Bird List v15.2 (Gill, Donsker & Rasmussen, eds.)
facts_sources.used_for: taxonomy: order Columbiformes, family Columbidae, Columba livia Gmelin, JF, 1789; 'Rock Dove' as English name and 'Feral Pigeon' for introduced populations

facts_sources.title: Goller, F. & Larsen, O. N. (1997) In situ biomechanics of the syrinx and sound generation in pigeons. Journal of Experimental Biology 200(16): 2165-2176
facts_sources.used_for: lateral tympaniform membranes as the sound source; tracheolateralis and sternotrachealis muscles; muscles mainly modulatory

facts_sources.title: Riede, T., Beckers, G. J. L., Blevins, W. & Suthers, R. A. (2004) Inflation of the esophagus and vocal tract filtering in ring doves. Journal of Experimental Biology 207: 4025-4036
facts_sources.used_for: beak and nostrils closed; upper oesophagus inflates; trachea and oesophagus filter out the 2nd and 3rd harmonics

facts_sources.title: Fletcher, N. H., Riede, T., Beckers, G. J. L. & Suthers, R. A. (2004) Vocal tract filtering and the 'coo' of doves. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America 116(6): 3750-3756
facts_sources.used_for: acoustic model: tuned trachea + glottal constriction + inflated oesophagus sac; sac radiates better than an open beak

facts_sources.title: Fletcher, N. H., Riede, T. & Suthers, R. A. (2006) Model for vocalization by a bird with distensible vocal cavity and open beak. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America 119(2): 1005-1011
facts_sources.used_for: dove pitch stays close to the inflated-sac resonance

facts_sources.title: Beckers, G. J. L., Suthers, R. A. & ten Cate, C. (2003) Mechanisms of frequency and amplitude modulation in ring dove song. Journal of Experimental Biology 206: 1833-1843
facts_sources.used_for: frequency modulation follows interclavicular air-sac pressure; limited frequency range in non-songbirds

facts_sources.title: Riede, T., Eliason, C. M., Miller, E. H., Goller, F. & Clarke, J. A. (2016) Coos, booms, and hoots: the evolution of closed-mouth vocal behavior in birds. Evolution 70(8): 1734-1746
facts_sources.used_for: rock dove listed as a closed-mouth vocaliser with oesophagus inflation, F0 about 400 Hz (Table S3); crop not inflated during calling
